rules: Only official sources (Parks Canada, Alberta Parks, BC Parks, park winter guides).
winter_activities lists only what a source names for this trail; empty means not recommended.
avalanche_exposure is set only from an official ATES rating for this trip; otherwise 'unknown'.
Trails not listed here keep the defaults: no winter activities, ATES unknown.
review_flag is for the human review only; the sync ignores it.

trails.name: Lake Agnes Tea House
trails.winter_notes: Parks Canada: not safe in winter (November to June) without avalanche training and equipment. The teahouses are closed in winter.
trails.review_flag: Not on Parks Canada's ATES lists; their Lake Louise page says avalanche terrain, so ATES stays unknown

trails.name: Johnston Canyon to the Ink Pots
trails.winter_access_note: From Oct 13, 2026 the canyon trail from the P1 lot is closed for maintenance. Reach the Upper Falls and Ink Pots from the Moose Meadows trailhead.
trails.winter_notes: Very icy; ice cleats strongly recommended.

trails.name: Plain of Six Glaciers
trails.winter_notes: Parks Canada: not safe in winter (November to June) without avalanche training and equipment. The teahouses are closed in winter.

trails.name: Sentinel Pass via Larch Valley
trails.winter_access_note: Moraine Lake Road is closed to vehicles in winter and becomes a ski and snowshoe trail. Past the Consolation Valley viewpoint it crosses large avalanche paths.

trails.name: Tunnel Mountain
trails.winter_notes: Steep and can be extremely icy. Poles and ice cleats strongly recommended.
trails.review_flag: Not ATES-rated; a low forested hill, but stays unknown (no official rating)

trails.name: Bow Glacier Falls
trails.winter_notes: Parks Canada rates the Bow Hut approach (same valley, past the falls) as Complex avalanche terrain.
trails.review_flag: ATES unknown: the falls themselves aren't rated

trails.name: Sunshine Meadows
trails.winter_notes: Parks Canada rates the Sunshine Village backcountry as Challenging avalanche terrain.
trails.review_flag: ATES unknown: the meadows trail isn't rated by name

trails.name: Consolation Lakes
trails.winter_access_note: Moraine Lake Road is closed to vehicles in winter and becomes a ski and snowshoe trail. Past the Consolation Valley viewpoint it crosses large avalanche paths.

trails.name: Skoki Valley Trail
trails.review_flag: Rated Simple ('Skoki via Boulder/Deception Passes') but it's a ski-touring trip, so no winter activities

trails.name: Eiffel Lake
trails.winter_access_note: Moraine Lake Road is closed to vehicles in winter and becomes a ski and snowshoe trail. Past the Consolation Valley viewpoint it crosses large avalanche paths.

trails.name: Shadow Lake - Twin Lakes - Redearth Creek Loop
trails.review_flag: Loop uses Redearth Creek (Challenging) and Twin Lakes from Hwy 1 (Simple): stored as the more severe

trails.name: Glacier Lake Trail
trails.review_flag: Rated Simple but not on any winter trail list

trails.name: Mount Assiniboine via Bryant Creek
trails.winter_notes: Parks Canada rates Bryant Creek as Simple; Assiniboine Pass beyond it isn't rated.
trails.review_flag: ATES unknown: only part of the route is rated

trails.name: Lake Minnewanka Shoreline Trail
trails.winter_notes: Can be very icy, especially in spring.
trails.winter_route_ends: Stewart Canyon bridge, 1.5 km from the Lake Minnewanka day-use area (3 km return).

trails.name: Taylor Lake
trails.review_flag: Rated Simple but not on any winter trail list

trails.name: Maligne Canyon
trails.winter_access_note: Closed until further notice after the 2024 Jasper wildfire.

trails.name: Valley of the Five Lakes
trails.winter_notes: Wetland Way, Emerald Circuit and Valley Loop are listed as winter walks.

trails.name: Wilcox Pass
trails.winter_access_note: Icefields Parkway: winter tires or chains required Nov 1 - Mar 31.
trails.winter_notes: Avalanche terrain exists beyond the Red Chairs. The pass itself is rated Challenging.
trails.winter_route_ends: The Red Chairs viewpoint (about 3.4 km return).

trails.name: Tonquin Valley
trails.review_flag: Astoria approach Simple, Portal Creek approach Challenging: stored as the more severe

trails.name: Bald Hills
trails.review_flag: 'Bald Hills area' Challenging; only the lookout trail to the hitching rail is Simple

trails.name: Jacques Lake
trails.winter_notes: User-tracked, not groomed.
trails.winter_route_ends: Beaver Lake (4 km return) or Summit Lakes (10 km return).

trails.name: Jonas Pass - Poboktan Creek
trails.winter_notes: Parks Canada rates Poboktan Creek as Simple; Jonas Pass isn't rated.

trails.name: Bertha Lake
trails.winter_notes: The trailhead is in an avalanche path. Check the daily Bertha-Townsite avalanche advisory.

trails.name: Crandell Lake
trails.winter_notes: Parks Canada lists it as a winter fat-bike trail off the Akamina Parkway.
trails.review_flag: Rated Simple; Parks Canada names it for fat biking, not walking or snowshoeing

trails.name: Goat Lake
trails.winter_access_note: Red Rock Parkway is closed to vehicles from November to May.

trails.name: Chester Lake
trails.winter_notes: The first 0.2 km is shared with skiers; then follow the snowshoe trail signs. Check the Alberta Parks trail report for closures before you go.

trails.name: Ptarmigan Cirque
trails.winter_access_note: Highway 40 is closed from Peter Lougheed Provincial Park to Highwood House junction, Dec 1 - Jun 14.

trails.name: Burstall Pass
trails.winter_notes: Alberta Parks shows avalanche terrain near Burstall Pass at treeline.
trails.review_flag: Only a photo caption ('Challenging Terrain'), not a formal rating: left unknown

trails.name: Tent Ridge Horseshoe
trails.winter_notes: Alberta Parks shows Tent Ridge as an example of Complex avalanche terrain.
trails.review_flag: Only a photo caption ('Complex Terrain'), not a formal rating: left unknown

trails.name: Elizabeth Parker Hut / Lake O'Hara
trails.winter_notes: Beyond the Ross Lake loop the Lake O'Hara Fire Road travels through avalanche zones (Parks Canada).
trails.review_flag: Rated Simple ('Lake O'Hara Road to Elizabeth Parker Hut') but it's a ski-touring approach: no activities

trails.name: Emerald Lake Loop
trails.winter_notes: There is a large avalanche slide path on the left side of the lake (Parks Canada).
trails.review_flag: ATES left unknown: only the nearby Nordic trails are rated Simple

trails.name: Stanley Glacier
trails.winter_notes: Parks Canada does not maintain or patrol winter trails in Kootenay.

trails.name: Eva Lake
trails.winter_access_note: Meadows in the Sky Parkway is closed to vehicles past the gate at the Welcome Kiosk in winter.

trails.name: Jade Lakes
trails.winter_access_note: Meadows in the Sky Parkway is closed to vehicles past the gate at the Welcome Kiosk in winter.

trails.name: Hermit Trail
trails.winter_notes: Many areas of Rogers Pass have restricted or prohibited access in winter.

trails.name: Joffre Lakes
trails.winter_access_note: Vehicle access is weather-dependent from November to May.
trails.winter_notes: BC Parks: in fall, winter and spring you are exposed to avalanche risk. Bring an avalanche transceiver, probe and shovel. No winter camping.

trails.name: Elfin Lakes
trails.winter_access_note: Chains are mandatory on the access road from October to May.
trails.winter_notes: BC Parks calls Diamond Head a backcountry touring area and expects avalanche training and gear (transceiver, probe, shovel).

trails.name: Garibaldi Lake
trails.winter_notes: BC Parks: avalanche and glacier hazards exist year-round.

trails.name: Cyprus Lake to the Grotto
trails.winter_access_note: Register your vehicle at the Cyprus Lake office. Snow tires recommended.
trails.winter_notes: Reach the Grotto by the Georgian Bay, Marr Lake or Horse Lake trails. Trails aren't maintained. The shoreline at the Grotto is icy: stay back from the edge.

trails.name: Gros Morne Mountain
trails.winter_notes: Parks Canada does not recommend climbing the mountain in winter: icy and treacherous. The Ferry Gulch section crosses active avalanche zones.

trails.name: Centennial Ridges
trails.winter_access_note: The road is closed in winter: park at the locked gate on Highway 60 (about 2 km each way).
trails.winter_notes: For experienced snowshoers; a difficult route.
trails.review_flag: Source is the park's winter guide PDF (Friends of Algonquin site)
